s0.p1: Background (parallel) threads in JavaScript are emulated using workers
s0.p2: How do you create a worker?
s0.p3: As always – using the constructor! [ico-20 wink]
s0.p4: Note that we pass a reference to the script file to the **Worker** constructor
s0.p5: The script contained in that file will run in parallel with the main thread
s0.p6: As the **worker**’s code runs in parallel with the main thread, it has no access to the DOM
s0.p7: The page is inaccessible to it...
s0.p8: However, it can output messages to the console
s0.p9: It can also interact with the main thread from which it was launched
s0.p10: To understand how it does this, let’s take a look at the prototype of its constructor
s0.p11: Right then, we (or rather, the **worker**) have at our disposal the inherited methods **postMessage** and **terminate** (quite ‘self-explanatory’ names)
s0.p12: as well as the properties **onmessage** and **onerror**
s0.p14: • in the **worker**’s code, you need to set up an **_message_** event handler, which will be triggered when messages are received from the main script
s0.p15: Like all event handlers, it receives an event object
s0.p16: This event will have a **data** property, which will contain the message sent by the main script
s0.p17: • You can send a message from the **worker** to the script in the main thread (which launched the **worker**)
s0.p18: • You can send a message from the main thread to the **worker**
s0.p19: Please note a very important point:
s0.p20: ![ico-20 warn] We are sending an array to the **worker**, not a string
s0.p21: ^^i.e. when exchanging data with a **worker** using **postMessage**, we do not need to use the **JSON.stringify** method^^
s0.p22: ^^as the data circulates within the browser rather than being sent via _http_^^
s0.p23: The importScripts method allows scripts to be imported into the body of the worker
s0.p24: In the following example, we’ll leave the main script unchanged,
s0.p25: and only modify the worker’s code:
s0.p26: The worker imports the Sha256 script, which it uses to generate a digest of the received message
s0.p27: The generated digest is sent back to the main script
